purpose: Prefer ordinary contemporary General American English where it preserves technical meaning. Resolve dense 561 terms through canonical resources before generation; this lexicon is not a synonym bank.
doNotFlatten: legal defined terms and operative modal verbs
implementation hypotheses that have not been verified as deployed behavior

rules: Resolve a dense term before expanding it into ordinary prose.
Raw corpus frequency never establishes canonical meaning or house style.
Preserve the canonical term when its technical distinction matters, then explain it at first consequential use.
Keep deprecated aliases as provenance and search keys; do not generate them as current canonical prose.
If a term cannot be resolved, mark it unresolved and keep the term instead of inventing a definition.

invariants: A semantic gloss is not a substitute for its canonical source.
A service office is not the same thing as the institutional body that contains it.
A governance decision is not the same thing as a scientific claim.
An implementation hypothesis is not a deployed capability.
A formal mathematical claim keeps its formal status during prose rendering.
ambiguityPolicy: When an ordinary synonym would erase a real technical distinction, keep the specialist term and resolve it from its canonical resource. If the resource is unavailable, mark the term unresolved instead of guessing.
